function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

2. In Los Angeles (LA) find Japanese sushi restaurants with delivery service.

But the function expects a string; we can pass "Japanese" or "Sushi". Let's pass "Japanese".

Preferences: ["Delivery"].

That means each function call must be a separate response. So we need to produce two responses: one calling restaurant_finder for New York, then another for Los Angeles. There's no instruction about combining them into one call. So we will produce two separate calls.

Thus first response: call restaurant_finder with arguments: location="New York, NY", cuisine="Italian", preferences=["Vegetarian"]. Then second response: call restaurant_finder with arguments: location="Los Angeles, CA", cuisine="Japanese", preferences=["Delivery"].
